newsitem.title: USA: Ku Klux Klan rallies in Pittsburgh.
newsitem.headline: Ku Klux Klan rallies in Pittsburgh.

text.p: Wearing their signature robes and hoods and waving Confederate and Nazi flags, the Ku Klux Klan rallied in Pittsburgh on Saturday before a hostile crowd that booed, jeered and threw stones.

About 40 Klan members dressed in both white and black robes and hoods stood on the steps of a downtown government building and using a sound system, told white Americans to "wake up" and prepare for a race war. They said African-Americans should be deported from the country.
"America's salvation is (black) deportation," said C. Edward Foster, the KKK's Grand Dragon. "That's what it's all about, America, white revolution."
A crowd of nearly 2,000 people, both black and white, booed, threw stones, and shouted "Klan go home" in unison.
One spectator was arrested but there was no major violence.
The crowd was contained behind a six-foot high fence, and a four-foot high fence enclosed the area where Klan members stood. Police in riot gear lined the streets.
Using frequent racial slurs, Klan members denegrated blacks, Jews and homosexuals, and attacked the media for portraying the KKK as a hate group.
The KKK won the right to rally in Pittsburgh last month when a federal judge ruled the city could not stop them because it would violate the First Amendment.
The city had denied the KKK a permit to demonstrate and the white supremacist group in turn sued the city.
